note: Establish the main carbon-number cuts and measure blend purity, recovery, and column economics before adding more separation.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a high-value backbone first: split C4-and-lighter / C5 / C6 / C7+; inspect recoveries and costs, then add light-end and heavy-end polishing only where profitable. Step 1: three-column backbone.
Root splits at C4/C5, B at C5/C6, BB at C6/C7. Moderate stages/reflux and pressure let to avoid costly tall/high-duty columns. C5 and C6 streams are initially intended as blends; later separate C6 paraffins from naphthenes.

note: Rebuild around sharp C5/C6 split and five high-value blend outlets; defer C7+ separation until the backbone economics are visible.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a high-value backbone first: split C5/C6 at root, recover C3/C4/C5 blends in the light branch, and C6 paraffin/naphthene blends in the heavy branch; then add C7+ polishing and optimize costs. Step 2: six-column blend plant.
First attempt showed sloppy C4/C5, C5/C6, C6/C7 cuts and no sellable streams; root cost was $224M/yr. Sharp C5/C6 root avoids losing valuable pentanes. Light branch: T splits C3/C4, TT removes ethane (needed because 34 mol/s would otherwise contaminate C3 blend), TB separates C4 and C5 blends. Heavy branch: B splits C6/C7; BT splits paraffins from naphthenes. Sell BB as mixed C7+ for now.

note: Sharpen the root and all downstream cuts to recover the large C5 and C6 blend values, accepting one expensive iteration to establish a saleable backbone.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a high-value backbone: sharp C5/C6 root, C3/C4/C5 blends above and C6 paraffin/naphthene blends below; then add C7+ recovery and optimize costs. Step 3: sharpen all six cuts.
Current six-column plant earns $375M but costs $533M. Main losses: root sends ~210 mol/s N-pentane into BTT, while BTB is only 87% C6 paraffin. Light cuts also leak badly. Root 80/5 should approach ideal 1559 mol/s C5-lighter tops (R81 got 1500); higher reflux downstream should recover C5 and C6 blends. Expensive root is unavoidable but later reduce stages/reflux after purity is achieved.

note: Rebuild around the easiest C4/C5 split and a direct C5 blend outlet, using much cheaper columns to establish positive economics.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a cheap sequential C4/C5 then C5/C6 backbone for the valuable C5 blend; add C6 blend recovery only if marginal revenue beats cost, then optimize. Step 1: test low-cost two-column C5 recovery.
The prior six-column plant earns only $389M and costs $815M; sharpening cannot rescue its economics. Root 80/5 costs $350M. C4/C5 is an easier first cut than C5/C6 and lets the second column produce C5 blend directly. Test 50/2/3 root and 50/3/4 heavy split, with all other branches sold. R127 confirms 60/3/3 root costs $225M, so duties/stages must be much lower for profitability.

note: Remove the worthless heavy split and sharpen the C4/C5 column so the existing root's C5-rich tops become a saleable C5 blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable two-column C5-blend plant first; then either tune these cuts or test a single high-value pure-product branch. Current step: split the existing C4+C5 tops sharply and discard all unsold heavy branches.
The existing root already makes a C4+C5 tops stream (about 603 mol/s C5, 87% feed recovery), so its heavy column is wasted. R173 shows C5 blend can earn $386M/yr even with incomplete recovery. R174's 50/2.5/2.5 C4/C5 splitter leaves 43% butane in bottoms; use reflux 4 and boil-up 5 to strip C4 overhead. Root cost is $202M and a modest second column should leave substantial profit if C5 exceeds 95%.

note: Adopt the profitable C6-paraffin backbone and intensify only the C4/C5 polishing column to make its C5-rich bottoms saleable.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the best proven C6-paraffin backbone, then turn its C5-rich TB stream into a second saleable blend while controlling polishing cost. Current step: copy R268 and strengthen only its light polishing column.
R268 earns $1119M/yr from a 96% C6-paraffin BT stream with reward 0.885. Its TB stream is 88% C5, with 9% N-butane and 3% DMB; much stronger C4/C5 separation should unlock roughly $500M/yr more revenue. Root and B remain unchanged. Avoid further heavy-end splitting until both blend products are secure.

note: Adopt the 1.716-reward backbone and cut the C4/C5 polisher boil-up sharply to stop losing roughly 227 mol/s of C5 overhead, with extra reflux preserving C4 rejection.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R314's profitable four-column C6/C5 backbone, then improve the C4/C5 polisher recovery without losing the C5 blend specification. Current step: copy R314 and reduce its excessive C5 carryover into TBT by lowering boil-up while raising reflux.
R314 earns 1.716 with $1536M/yr revenue: C6 paraffin $1119M and C5 $417M. Its TB polisher sends 299 mol/s overhead, including about 227 mol/s saleable C5, although only about 72 mol/s N-butane needs removal. Lower boil-up should retain much more C5 in TBB; higher reflux should still reject C4. Root and B produce the proven 96% C6 blend and remain unchanged. Avoid heavy-end splitting until light recovery is optimized.

note: Add the proven C3/C4 splitter to monetize the light bottoms while preserving the improved C5 recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Retain the profitable four-column C6/C5 backbone, monetize the light C4 stream, then reduce dominant column costs and test further recovery only where net positive. Current step: add R361's proven C3/C4 splitter to my improved C5-recovery design.
My TB=70/6/1.2/0.1 improves C5 blend revenue to $567M and reward to 2.113; TBT is only 121 mol/s. R361's TT=70/4/4/0 converts 793 mol/s TT into a $149M C4 blend for $51M/yr cost, so it should add about 0.22 reward here. Root, B and T are expensive ($731M combined); after securing C4 revenue, optimize these rather than adding marginal heavy-end columns.

note: Reduce the oversized C6/heavy splitter substantially while preserving its pressure and cut; this isolates whether the C6 blend can remain saleable at much lower capital and energy cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Retain the profitable C6/C5/C4 backbone, reduce the dominant root/B/T column costs without losing blend specifications, then test only clearly profitable recovery additions. Current step: intensify-cost-optimize B, whose 110-stage/6-reflux column costs $278.5M/yr yet produces a nearly pure C6-paraffin blend.
Current reward 2.337; revenue $1835M, costs $810M. TB=70/6/1.2/0.1 gives high-recovery $567M C5 blend; TT=70/4/4 adds $149M C4 blend for $51M. Unsold heavy and C3 streams are low-value or require multiple columns, so cost reduction has priority. Test B=70/4/5/0.15 first; downstream is unchanged, making this a clean one-solve economic test.

note: Combine the two validated splitter reductions: R456's less costly C6/heavy column and R458's less costly C4/C5 column should retain all three blend sales.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine the best independently validated cost reductions, then optimize the dominant root and B columns while preserving blend specifications. Current step: combine R456's cheaper B with R458's cheaper T in one design.
R456 (2.466) shows B=100/5/6 retains C6 purity and cuts B cost by $40M. R458 (2.461) shows T=70/4/5 retains both C4/C5 sales and cuts T cost by $52M. Combining should save about $92M versus the 2.337 baseline with little recovery loss. Next test B or root reductions individually; TT intensification destroyed C4 sales, so avoid.

note: Recover the substantial cyclohexane/MCP value in BB: harder stripping in B should remove n-hexane contamination, while a new BB splitter targets a saleable C6-naphthene tops blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 backbone, reduce major column costs where safe, and now test recovery of the valuable C6 naphthenes currently lost in BB. Current step: strip residual light C6 from BB harder and add a cyclohexane/heptane splitter.
Current best 2.529: revenue 1827, cost718. BT C6-paraffin blend earns1109 but is only ~95% pure; TBB C5 earns570 and TTB C4 earns148. Root/B dominate cost. BB contains ~186 cyclohexane and ~41 MCP, potentially ~$397M/yr as naphthene blend, plus ~38 n-hexane contamination. Increasing B boil-up should strip n-hexane into BT; a new BB column may then sell a naphthene tops blend. Avoid TT intensification: it previously destroyed C4 sales, and C3 value is too small.

note: Restore the best backbone and probe the narrow operating window between boil-up 6 and 8: enough stripping to clean the heavy stream without losing the C6 paraffin blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the 2.529 backbone, find an intermediate heavy-splitter boil-up that preserves C6 sales while removing more n-hexane from BB, then recover cyclohexane/heptane/octane only if the heavy feeds become separable. Current step: test B boil-up 6.5 with the existing BB cut.
Best 2.529 = R506: revenue1827, cost718; products BT C6 1109, TBB C5 570, TTB C4 148. B boil6 gives C6 blend 95% but BB has 5% n-hexane; boil8 strips hexane but loses C6 blend (BT only89% paraffins). BB70/4/4 splits cyclohexane/heptane poorly, so do not intensify blindly. A moderate 6.5 may preserve BT and improve BB. Avoid TT changes and low-margin C3 recovery.

note: Adopt R603 and trim the two light splitters moderately; the C4 cut has substantial purity margin, while the C5 cut is left with a conservative setting.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the best 2.561 backbone, then shave cost only where product purity has margin; avoid heavy-train additions until a clearly profitable separation is demonstrated. Current step: modestly reduce both light splitters while retaining the C4 and C5 blend outlets.
Best known R603=2.561: revenue1827.9, cost704.9; B=100/5/6/.15 is near the C6 95% boundary and must stay fixed. Root is costly but changing its cut risks all products. T=60/3.5/4.5 and TT=70/4/4 work; C4 bottoms are essentially all blend while C5 bottoms are near 95%, so make only moderate reductions. Heavy BB cuts tested at 70/4/4 and 80/5/5 do not yield pure products; boil-up >6 in B destroys the valuable C6 blend. Ignore C3 recovery (about $73M gross) and side draws unless economics become compelling.

note: Combine the profitable TBT N-butane recovery with the validated low-cost C3/C4 splitter; both changes are independently proven and affect separate branches.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine the validated TBT recovery column with the cheaper C3/C4 splitter, then make only conservative cuts to columns whose products have purity margin. Current step: test R651 with TT=40/2.5/3.
R651 earns 2.600 by adding TBT=50/3/3/.1: TBTT is premium N-butane worth $25.0M at only $7.7M cost. R652 shows TT=40/2.5/3 still gives a fully C4 bottoms blend and saves $13.4M versus 70/4/4. Combining should yield about 2.62. B=100/5/6/.15 is extremely sensitive: 95/4.75/6 loses the entire $1109M C6 blend. Root and T cuts also risk all blend products. Heavy train attempts are uneconomic; C3 recovery needs multiple separations for only ~$73M gross. Next, if valid, cautiously reduce TT or TBT further.

note: Adopt R698's proven TBT boil-up increase: it converts both small outlets into saleable products and raises reward to 2.742 without touching the sensitive main splitters.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R698's validated TBT boil-up increase, then use remaining solves for conservative improvements with clear upside and limited risk to the large blend revenues.
R698 earns 2.742: raising TBT boil-up from 3.0 to 4.5 makes both outlets saleable (premium N-butane $30.1M and C5 blend $47.8M) for only $1.6M extra cost, a $52.9M revenue gain. Keep root, B, T and TB fixed: prior tests show their cuts are highly sensitive and can destroy the $1109M C6 or $571M C5 blends. TT=40/2.5/3 is validated. TBT=30/2/2 loses premium and bottoms value. Heavy recovery and extra C3 trains have been uneconomic. Next probe modest TBT cost/operating refinements around 50/3/4.5.

note: Adopt R745's proven C3 train and raise only its small C3/C4 splitter boil-up, seeking to recover the substantial C3 currently lost in its bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the profitable two-column C3 train, then increase its small C3/C4 splitter boil-up to recover more of the 111 mol/s C3 currently lost to its unsold bottoms while retaining 95% C3 overhead.
R745 earns 2.787 by adding TTT ethane rejection and TTTB C3/C4 splitting: $35.3M extra revenue for $15.1M cost. Its TTTBT is pure C3 but only 138 mol/s, while TTTBB still contains about 111 mol/s propane/propylene. A modest boil-up increase should move much of that C3 overhead; the column costs only $4.2M/yr, so upside outweighs energy cost. Keep all major blend-producing columns unchanged.

note: Continue the successful C3-recovery direction: boil-up 4.5 improved both revenue and reward, and the bottoms still contain roughly 80 mol/s of C3.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the inexpensive C3/C4 polisher first; then use remaining solves for conservative cost trims on the dominant blend splitters if the purity margin permits.
Current best is 2.803 at TTTB reflux 2.5/boil-up 4.5. Raising boil-up from 3.0 to 4.5 increased C3 product from 138 to 168 mol/s and reward by 0.016, while overhead remains 100% C3. R795's 4.0 was worse and R796's higher reflux was worse, so heat—not reflux—is the useful direction. TTTBB still has about 80 mol/s C3, so test 5.5. Major blend columns are proven and should remain fixed; heavy BB has resisted prior splitting attempts.

note: Adopt the island-best 2.814 design and trim the large C6/heavy splitter from 100 to 95 stages; the C6 blend has full purity margin, so modest capital savings should be retained.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the best C3 setting, then spend the final solves on conservative stage-count trims of the three dominant blend splitters, checking product purity after each change.
R844 reaches 2.814 at TTTB boil-up 6.0, still improving C3 recovery over 5.5. The main costs are feed $268M, B $239M and T $119M. All saleable blend streams have useful purity margin, especially BT (100% C6 paraffins) and TTB (100% C4). Test B at 95 stages first; its C6 blend should remain robust, while even modest size savings exceed the remaining C3 polishing gains. Heavy BB remains unsold and prior attempts to monetize it failed.

note: Restore the island-best 2.841 design exactly; its heavier-column pressure increase and C3 boil-up increase are both independently profitable, unlike the failed stage trim.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R888 as the best proven design, then use the remaining solve capacity only for a conservative heavy-splitter pressure test if budget permits.
R888 reaches 2.841: B at 100 stages and pressure drop 0.25 improves C6 recovery enough to outweigh its higher cost, and TTTB boil-up 8.0 gives the best C3 recovery observed. Do not repeat the failed 95-stage B trim, which made BT unsaleable. Feed, T, and other splitters are unchanged and proven.

note: Adopt island-best R934 and spend the final two solves extending both profitable trends: lower B operating pressure for additional C6 recovery and higher small-column boil-up for additional C3 recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Use the final two solves to extend the two independently profitable recovery trends from island-best R934, then stop.
R934 scores 2.857 with B pressure drop 0.35 and TTTB boil-up 9.0. Increasing B pressure drop from 0.25 to 0.30 to 0.35 has consistently recovered more saleable C6 blend, while higher TTTB boil-up consistently recovers more C3 at negligible cost. Test B dp 0.40 and boil-up 10.0 together; R934 remains the proven fallback if this final probe does not improve.
